elements.label: Table 4.2. Human Capital Index disaggregated by gender
elements.description:
| HCI component | Indicator | MALE 2010 | MALE 2020 | FEMALE 2010 | FEMALE 2020 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HCI Component 1: Survival | Probability of survival to age 5 | 0.973 | 0.976 | 0.981 | 0.983 |
| HCI Component 2: School | Expected years of schooling | 11.7 | 12.5 | 11.9 | 13.2 |
| HCI Component 2: School | Harmonized test scores | 530 | 514 | 536 | 524 |
| HCI Component 3: Health | Survival rate from age 15-60 | 0.808 | 0.813 | 0.92 | 0.924 |
| HCI Component 3: Health | Fraction of children under 5 not stunted | 0.763 | 0.752 | 0.784 | 0.773 |
| | Human Capital Index | 0.63 | 0.65 | 0.68 | 0.73 |

Note: Maximum harmonized test score is 625. Source: World Bank HCI.

elements.label: Figure 4.8. School Attendance by age and gender, 2020
elements.description: Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: School attendance rate (%), scale 0 to 100 in steps of 20. X-axis categories: 10–14, 15–19, 20–24. Legend: Female (teal), Male (orange). No values are printed on the bars; approximate readings: 10–14: Female ~97, Male ~96; 15–19: Female ~74, Male ~70; 20–24: Female ~26, Male ~27. Attendance falls sharply with age for both genders, and the gender gap is small, with females slightly ahead at ages 10–14 and 15–19 and roughly equal at ages 20–24. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2020.
